tag_t8.block.grund.zusammenarbeit: Considers cooperation more important than its reservations.

tag_t8.block.grund.migration: Worried about border protection and readmissions.

tag_t8.block.brics.label: Become a BRICS partner country
tag_t8.block.brics.hinweis: The South opens markets and financing (Russia, China, India, Brazil, South Africa, the Emirates); Washington and Brussels read it as turning away from the West: trust among NATO and EU states falls, foreign capital hesitates.
tag_t8.block.brics.schon: Turkey is already a partner country.
tag_t8.block.ots.label: Host a summit of the Turkic states
tag_t8.block.ots.hinweis: The Middle Corridor, arms deals and trade among the Turkic states; Moscow and Beijing view it with suspicion.
tag_t8.block.fehlt.spiel: There is no foreign policy without a running game.
tag_t8.block.brics.text: Turkey becomes a BRICS partner country: Moscow, Beijing, New Delhi and Brasília welcome the step, Washington and Brussels react with irritation.
tag_t8.block.brics.why: Costs {pk} capital. Trust falls in {n} NATO and EU states; foreign capital hesitates, exports and markets in the South gain.
tag_t8.block.brics.titel: Turkey becomes a BRICS partner country
tag_t8.block.ots.text: The summit of the Turkic states in Istanbul brings pledges on the Middle Corridor and on joint defence projects.
tag_t8.block.ots.why: Costs {pk} capital. Moscow and Beijing view the growing ties with suspicion.
daten.dienst.op.kandidat.name: Support a camp in an election campaign
daten.dienst.op.kandidat.text: Money, media access and networks for one camp in the target state. Strongest in the months before the election, and even then only limited: voters decide for themselves, and an exposed involvement often strengthens the other side.
daten.dienst.op.desinfo.name: Disinformation campaign
daten.dienst.op.desinfo.text: Targeted false reports and rumours weaken the target state's leadership. Cheap and quick, but easy to expose.
daten.dienst.op.netz.name: Build an influence network
daten.dienst.op.netz.text: Ties to politics, media and business: it takes time, but brings access that makes later operations easier and less likely to be exposed.
daten.dienst.op.cyber.name: Intelligence and cyber
daten.dienst.op.cyber.text: Insight into the target state's situation and intentions: election prospects, stability — and whether foreign operations against Turkey are under way.
daten.dienst.op.gegen.name: Step up counter-intelligence
daten.dienst.op.gegen.text: Keeps foreign operations against Turkey small and makes their discovery more likely. Works against all states at once.
daten.dienst.op.gruppen.name: Support groups abroad
daten.dienst.op.gruppen.text: Money, advice and backing for a group in the target state that harries its leadership. Weakens stability there, is hard to steer and not seldom backfires: whoever strengthens groups does not control what they do later.
daten.dienst.op.cyberangriff.name: Cyberattack on state agencies
daten.dienst.op.cyberangriff.text: Disrupts the target state's administration and services for a while and breaks off its ongoing operations against Turkey. Quick, but traces on the network often lead back, and the counterstrike hits our own networks.

daten.konflikt.arm_aze.text: The peace treaty has been initialled since August 2025 but not signed: Baku is waiting for the Armenian referendum, Yerevan for Ankara to open the border. Ankara keeps its own border closed as leverage — and would be the biggest beneficiary of the corridor.
daten.konflikt.ukr_rus.text: The war is frozen, not over: the Istanbul rounds, the exchange in Abu Dhabi and the failed Geneva round lie behind us, and each ceasefire broke within days. Ankara has the grain plan in its drawer and leads the maritime security component — success here is the biggest prestige lever in the game.
daten.konflikt.isr_irn.titel: Israel and Iran: the Hormuz fallout
daten.konflikt.isr_irn.text: The war between Israel, the USA and Iran has been halted, not resolved, since the 60-day ceasefire of the Islamabad Memorandum: Hormuz stays closed and the oil price squeezes every importer — Turkey is the main victim outside the warring parties. Qatar and Oman are already mediating; Ankara would be a host with its own economic interest.
daten.konflikt.lby_fraktionen.text: Libya is divided without being at war: the duopoly of Tripoli and the East keeps the 2020 ceasefire, but no state grows together. Ankara is the only outside actor with a line to both camps — trainers and drones in the West, growing contacts in the East.

daten.konflikt.forderung.arm_aze.a.0: Opening the border and the Gyumri–Kars railway as the first visible step
daten.konflikt.forderung.arm_aze.a.1: The TRIPP link to Nakhchivan runs under Armenian law and Armenian sovereignty
daten.konflikt.forderung.arm_aze.b.0: A constitutional amendment in Armenia before signing: no more territorial claim in the basic law
daten.konflikt.forderung.arm_aze.b.1: Unhindered access to Nakhchivan via the TRIPP corridor
daten.konflikt.forderung.ukr_rus.a.0: Security guarantees before any talk of territorial questions
daten.konflikt.forderung.ukr_rus.a.1: A complete exchange of prisoners and of the deported children
daten.konflikt.forderung.ukr_rus.b.0: Negotiating the status of the occupied territories from the current lines
daten.konflikt.forderung.ukr_rus.b.1: Steps on sanctions and an official channel to Europe
daten.konflikt.forderung.isr_irn.a.0: Opening the Strait of Hormuz to everyone's trade
daten.konflikt.forderung.isr_irn.a.1: A lasting ceasefire and an end to attacks through proxies
daten.konflikt.forderung.isr_irn.b.0: Steps on sanctions and the blockade before Hormuz is opened
daten.konflikt.forderung.isr_irn.b.1: Payment of the funds released under the Islamabad Memorandum
Recognition as the government of the whole country, not as the administration of the West
Oil revenues flow through the central bank in Tripoli
Its own access to oil revenues and posts in the central institutions
Security control in the East stays in its own hands
daten.konflikt.rot.arm_aze.a.0: No transit regime on the Zangezur section that overrides Armenian sovereignty
daten.konflikt.rot.arm_aze.b.0: No signing of the peace treaty without a prior constitutional amendment in Yerevan
daten.konflikt.rot.ukr_rus.a.0: No recognition of the annexations under international law
daten.konflikt.rot.isr_irn.a.0: No agreement that locks in Tehran's advance towards the bomb
daten.konflikt.rot.isr_irn.b.0: No opening of Hormuz without prior steps on sanctions
daten.konflikt.rot.lby_fraktionen.a.0: No permanent division of the country
daten.konflikt.rot.lby_fraktionen.b.0: No disarmament of its own forces without international guarantees
daten.konflikt.hebel.arm_aze.tripp.label: TRIPP corridor
daten.konflikt.hebel.arm_aze.tripp.text: Transit to Nakhchivan across Armenian territory.
daten.konflikt.hebel.arm_aze.tripp.richt: Opening against sovereignty: the link is coming, the question is whose law applies on it — from full Armenian control to an international regime.
Referendum in Armenia and signing of the peace treaty.
Baku signs after the constitutional amendment, Yerevan wants it the other way round; in between lies a roadmap of steps and counter-steps.
daten.konflikt.hebel.arm_aze.grenze.text: Border opening for third-country nationals, the Gyumri–Kars railway, the Ani bridge.
daten.konflikt.hebel.arm_aze.grenze.rich: Partial opening now against full opening after signing — the more happens in advance, the less pressure rests on the referendum.
daten.konflikt.hebel.ukr_rus.getreide.te: Grain and fertiliser through the Black Sea; ports and insurers are working again.
daten.konflikt.hebel.ukr_rus.getreide.ri: From a limited grain window (model 2022: 33 million t) to a permanent trade corridor with inspections — it never drags the territorial question along.
daten.konflikt.hebel.ukr_rus.gefangene.t: Exchange formats modelled on the 1,000-for-1,000 swap in Istanbul.
daten.konflikt.hebel.ukr_rus.gefangene.r: Small, repeatable rounds build trust for everything bigger — the one direction that never costs either side anything.
daten.konflikt.hebel.ukr_rus.meerengen.t: The Montreux rules and the maritime security component under Turkish leadership.
daten.konflikt.hebel.ukr_rus.meerengen.r: Calm at sea against calm at the front: a ceasefire on the water is easier to hold than one on the line.
daten.konflikt.hebel.isr_irn.hormus.text: Tehran ties the opening to an end of the blockade and to sanctions.
daten.konflikt.hebel.isr_irn.hormus.rich: Opening against steps on sanctions: from the symbolic passage of single convoys to full reopening on a timetable — never for free.
daten.konflikt.hebel.isr_irn.gelder.text: The roughly $24 billion of the Islamabad Memorandum as a repeatable format.
daten.konflikt.hebel.isr_irn.gelder.rich: Money against extending the ceasefire: each tranche buys weeks of calm — a swap both sides can repeat.
daten.konflikt.hebel.isr_irn.kanal.label: Mediation channels
daten.konflikt.hebel.isr_irn.kanal.text: Qatar and Oman are already mediating; Ankara would offer a larger table.
daten.konflikt.hebel.isr_irn.kanal.richt: From a technical channel to the Istanbul format: the more parties at one table, the costlier it is for spoilers to go it alone.
daten.konflikt.hebel.lby_fraktionen.einn: The revenues flow, but both sides see how they are shared.
From a trust account with two keys to a sharing formula with international audit — money is the one lever both need.
daten.konflikt.hebel.lby_fraktionen.memo: The Turkish–Libyan memorandum of 2019 as the anchor of the partnership.
Ankara's gain: ratification in return for the mediator's role — the firmer the memorandum, the more weight the mediator carries.
daten.konflikt.hebel.lby_fraktionen.sich: Training and joint structures instead of rival forces.
From parallel training programmes to a joint council of the security forces — never the disarmament of one side.
daten.konflikt.paket.arm_aze.0: Roadmap: referendum first, then signing of the peace treaty
daten.konflikt.paket.arm_aze.1: TRIPP transit under Armenian sovereignty with international monitoring
daten.konflikt.paket.arm_aze.2: Border opening for third-country nationals and the Gyumri–Kars railway
daten.konflikt.paket.ukr_rus.1: Grain and trade corridor in the Black Sea
daten.konflikt.paket.ukr_rus.2: Straits rules under Montreux with Turkish monitoring
daten.konflikt.paket.isr_irn.0: Gradual opening of the Strait of Hormuz against a sanctions timetable
daten.konflikt.paket.isr_irn.1: Extension of the ceasefire against payment of further tranches
daten.konflikt.paket.isr_irn.2: Istanbul format: all channels at one table
daten.konflikt.paket.lby_fraktionen.0: Oil revenue trust with two keys
daten.konflikt.paket.lby_fraktionen.1: Regular meetings of both camps' security forces in Istanbul
daten.konflikt.spoiler.provokation.label: Provocation at the negotiating table
daten.konflikt.spoiler.provokation.text: {seite} flexes its muscles: an incident on the line, a speech for the home crowd — betting that the table in Istanbul will collapse.
daten.konflikt.spoiler.hardliner.label: Hardliners gain the upper hand
daten.konflikt.spoiler.hardliner.text: In {seite} the hardliners win a round: anyone who speaks of compromise is suddenly called a traitor there, and the negotiating delegation loses its mandate.
daten.konflikt.spoiler.sabotage.label: Sabotage from outside
daten.konflikt.spoiler.sabotage.text: A third power that profits from the conflict torpedoes the rapprochement: leaks, arms deliveries to the spoilers, a staged incident.
daten.konflikt.spoiler.ultimatum.label: Unilateral hardening of demands
daten.konflikt.spoiler.ultimatum.text: {seite} publicly hardens its conditions: what was negotiable yesterday is declared a precondition — an ultimatum that narrows the zone of the possible.
daten.konflikt.garantie.ueberwachung.tex: Turkish observers and a joint reporting office watch over compliance: small, lasting, unarmed.
daten.konflikt.garantie.ueberwachung.ris: Every reported violation lands on the guarantor's desk — small, but constant.
daten.konflikt.garantie.wirtschaft.label: Economic anchor
daten.konflikt.garantie.wirtschaft.text: A corridor on the grain model: Turkish ports, insurers and banks carry both sides' trade — a trade bonus and prestige for Ankara.
daten.konflikt.garantie.wirtschaft.risik: The anchor holds only as long as both sides deliver; if the corridor breaks, the guarantor loses face.
daten.konflikt.garantie.militaer.label: Military guarantee
daten.konflikt.garantie.militaer.text: Ankara guarantees the agreement militarily: trainers, observers and the pledge to intervene in an emergency.
daten.konflikt.garantie.militaer.risiko: The greatest effect, the greatest risk: a violation forces intervention — or a loss of face for the guarantor.
daten.konflikt.vorbereitung.kanaele.hinw: Discreet channels to both sides: intelligence to intelligence, foreign ministry to foreign ministry. Nobody loses face, everyone listens.
daten.konflikt.vorbereitung.vertrauensma: Small, verifiable steps: a prisoner exchange, a humanitarian corridor, a ceasefire on one section. Whoever delivers small can deliver big.
daten.konflikt.vorbereitung.gastgeber.hi: A formal summit offer on the model of Istanbul 2022: Ankara provides the venue, the format and discretion. The invitation alone shows leadership.
daten.vorhaben.verlierer.wunder_kappadok: Balloon operators and hoteliers in Göreme
daten.vorhaben.verlierer.bio_saatgut.ver: Smallholders who depend on saving their own seed
tag_t8.verm.zopa.unreif: The situation is not ripe ({reif} of {noetig} needed): the pain of the stalemate does not yet outweigh the compromise.
tag_t8.verm.zopa.misstrauen: {name} does not yet trust Ankara enough as a mediator ({wert} of {noetig}).
tag_t8.verm.zopa.breit: The situation is ripe ({reif}), and both sides trust Ankara to broker a settlement.
tag_t8.verm.zopa.schmal: There is a zone of possible agreement, but it is narrow: ripeness {reif}, trust {vertrauen}.
tag_t8.verm.grund.kapital: There is not enough capital for this.
tag_t8.verm.grund.wieder: Possible again in {n, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}.
tag_t8.verm.grund.misstrauen: {name} does not yet trust Ankara enough as a mediator.
tag_t8.verm.grund.einigung: The agreement stands — now implementation counts (guarantees and fending off spoilers).
tag_t8.verm.grund.keineZopa: There is no zone of possible agreement; the situation has to ripen first.
tag_t8.verm.grund.vorbereitungErledigt: The agreement stands; preparation is no longer needed.
tag_t8.verm.grund.gipfel: A summit is only worthwhile once there is a zone of possible agreement.
tag_t8.verm.grund.garantieSteht: A guarantee is already in place.
tag_t8.verm.grund.garantieZuSpaet: The agreement stands; a guarantee added afterwards has no effect.
tag_t8.verm.grund.angebotLiegt: The offer “{label}” is already on the table — only a mediation attempt decides.
tag_t8.verm.grund.garantieOhneZopa: Without a zone of possible agreement a guarantee is worthless.
tag_t8.verm.kipp.0.titel: Mediation {titel}: the process threatens to freeze
tag_t8.verm.kipp.0.text: The ripeness of the situation between {a} and {b} has fallen below {ende}. Without new channels and confidence-building measures Ankara's mediation becomes waste paper — and spoilers gain the upper hand.
tag_t8.verm.kipp.2.titel: Mediation {titel}: willingness to talk is growing
tag_t8.verm.kipp.2.text: The situation between {a} and {b} is ripening ({bereit}+): both sides are seriously weighing whether a compromise is cheaper than the stalemate. Now channels, confidence-building measures and the right moment count.
tag_t8.verm.kipp.3.titel: Mediation {titel}: the window for an agreement is opening
tag_t8.verm.kipp.3.text: Ripeness has reached {fenster}: the zone of possible agreement is as open as it rarely is. From ripeness {ab} a Turkish guarantee package can tip the balance — a summit and a mediation attempt now have their best prospects.
tag_t8.verm.geht_nicht: That is not possible right now.
tag_t8.verm.vorb.text: {label} between {namen}: the situation is ripening ({reif} of 100).
tag_t8.verm.vorb.why: Costs {pk} capital. Ripeness +{reif}; the road to the table gets shorter, but spoilers can set everything back.
tag_t8.verm.garantie.log: The prospects of the next mediation attempt rise by {n} points. If the agreement is concluded, the guarantee stands — with running costs and the risk of a breach.
tag_t8.verm.garantie.why: Costs {pk} capital. Prospects +{aussicht} points; if successful, the guarantee runs at {monat} capital a month. {risiko}
tag_t8.verm.ende.geordnet: The guarantee “{label}” between {namen} is wound up in an orderly way: the situation holds even without Ankara's backing.
tag_t8.verm.ende.bruch: Ankara withdraws the guarantee “{label}” in the middle of the conflict: both sides read it as a broken promise.
tag_t8.verm.ende.bruch.why: Prestige −2; whoever stands guarantor and then walks away loses face.
tag_t8.verm.fehlt.spiel: There is no mediation without a running game.
tag_t8.verm.erfolg.garantie: The Turkish guarantee “{label}” now stands — with running costs and the risk of a breach.
tag_t8.verm.erfolg.text: Mediation succeeds: {namen} agree on a package in Istanbul.
tag_t8.verm.erfolg.zeitung.fakt: {a} and {b} reach agreement through Turkish mediation: {paket}. The conflict index falls, Ankara's prestige grows.
tag_t8.verm.scheitern.gesicht: The guarantee package on offer does not convince: a loss of face (prestige {n}).
tag_t8.verm.scheitern.log: Both sides set conditions that are too high. Costs {pk} capital and some prestige; ripeness falls.{gesicht}
tag_t8.verm.scheitern.why: Costs {pk} capital and some prestige; ripeness falls by {n} points.{gesicht}
